_note: Myelinated mammalian neuron: a multi-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley cable. Channel kinetics follow Pospischil et al. 2008 (I_Na, I_Kd, I_L Ca) at a reference 36 C with a voltage-threshold V_T; the transient A-type K+ current uses Connor-Stevens 1971 kinetics; the hyperpolarization-activated I_h follows Destexhe et al. 1993; the Ca2+-activated K+ current (SK) is an instantaneous Hill function of [Ca2+]i. Morphology (node/internode densities, ~100x-diameter internode spacing, ~70 ohm-cm axoplasm) follows McIntyre-Richardson-Grill 2002; axial coupling is cable theory (Rall 1962). Gating is advanced by Rush-Larsen, V and concentrations by RK4. Units: V in mV, t in ms, length in um, currents in uA, conductances in mS, capacitance in uF, concentrations in mM; densities are per cm^2 and multiplied by each compartment's membrane area.

T.note: Body temperature (37 C); used for Nernst potentials.

Tref.note: Reference temperature (36 C) at which the gating rate equations are defined; Q10 scales kinetics away from this.

Q10.note: Temperature coefficient for gating kinetics; phi = Q10^((T-Tref)/10) divides every gating time constant.

cm.note: Specific membrane capacitance of unmyelinated membrane (node/soma/dendrite). Internodes use cm_myelin.

cm_myelin.note: Effective specific capacitance of a myelinated internode (myelin layers in series); ~25x lower than bare membrane.

Ri.note: Axoplasmic (cytoplasmic) resistivity; sets axial coupling conductance g_ax = (cross-sectional area)/(R_i * length).

Ko.note: Extracellular K+ (adjustable; raising it depolarizes E_K -> hyperkalemia).

Vrest.note: Target resting potential; the leak reversal E_leak is solved at build so total current is zero here.

VT.note: Spike-threshold shift parameter in the Na+/Kd rate equations; more negative lowers threshold.

ENa_note.note: Na+/K+/Ca2+ reversal potentials are computed from the Nernst equation each step from the dynamic concentrations.

E_K.note: Nominal K+ reversal (recomputed from concentrations); used for I_Kd, I_A, SK.

E_h.note: Reversal potential of the mixed-cation H-current.

E_leak.note: Passive leak reversal potential; together with the K+ channels it sets the resting potential near -68 mV.

SK_Kd.note: Half-activation [Ca2+]i of the Ca2+-activated K+ (SK) current (0.4 uM).

SK_n.note: Hill coefficient of SK Ca2+ activation.

density._note: Maximal conductance densities (mS/cm^2) per channel and region. Nodes/soma/hillock carry the active spiking conductances; internodes are nearly passive (myelin), with small shunt conductances. Dendrites carry sub-threshold channels (Ca, SK, A, h).

gNa_node.note: Fast Na+ density at nodes of Ranvier and the axon hillock (spike initiation/regeneration).

gNa_soma.note: Fast Na+ density at the soma.

gNa_dend.note: Fast Na+ density in dendrites (low; mostly passive/integrative).

gKd_soma.note: Delayed-rectifier K+ density at the soma.

gA.note: Transient A-type K+ density (soma + dendrites); delays firing and lengthens the inter-spike interval.

gCaL.note: High-threshold L-type Ca2+ density (soma + dendrites); raises [Ca2+]i during spikes to recruit SK.

gSK.note: Ca2+-activated K+ (SK) density (soma + dendrites); the source of spike-frequency adaptation.

gH.note: Hyperpolarization-activated cation (I_h) density (soma + dendrites); produces sag and rebound.

gLeak.note: Passive leak density of bare membrane; E_leak is solved so rest is a fixed point.

gLeak_inter.note: Leak density under myelin (high membrane resistance).

iMax.note: Maximal electrogenic Na+/K+-ATPase current density. Net outward (3 Na+ out / 2 K+ in per cycle = +1 charge out). Activated by [Na]i and [K]o.

Km_Nai.note: Half-activation internal Na+ for the pump.

n_Na.note: Hill coefficient for internal Na+ activation.

Km_Ko.note: Half-activation external K+ for the pump.

buffer.note: Effective ionic buffering / submembrane-shell factor: per-compartment ion changes are scaled by 1/beta, representing buffering and the thin sub-membrane shell that actually equilibrates on the spike timescale.

kRelax.note: Slow homeostatic relaxation of [Na]i/[K]i back to rest (tau ~ 0.7 s), representing longer-timescale regulation; small enough that single spikes still move ions.

caRelax.note: Lumped Ca2+ buffering/uptake relaxation rate toward resting [Ca2+]i.

dLong.note: Longitudinal diffusion coupling of intracellular ions between neighbouring compartments (smooths local depletion).

geometry._note: Lengths and diameters in micrometres; counts are integers. Compartment order: dendrite x n_dend, soma, hillock, then (node, internode) repeated with a node at both ends of the myelinated axon.

node_L.note: Node-of-Ranvier compartment length. Coarsened above the ~1 um anatomical node so the explicit cable integrator stays stable (node and internode capacitances are comparable); the node/internode membrane distinction that produces saltatory conduction is preserved.

internode_L.note: Myelinated internode compartment length (coarsened from the ~100 um anatomical internode to keep the explicit cable stable).

n_nodes.note: Number of nodes of Ranvier; internodes = n_nodes - 1.

amplitude.note: Default current-clamp stimulus amplitude (injected, inward-positive) at the chosen compartment.

bcl.note: Default basic cycle length for periodic pacing.

gE.note: Peak excitatory (AMPA-like) synaptic conductance on the dendrite; reversal 0 mV.

gI.note: Peak inhibitory (GABA-like) synaptic conductance on the dendrite; reversal -75 mV.
